title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap details, opt-in default, licensing guidance and documented controls are supported. The creation path stops at the wizard rather than the site-selection control, although the accompanying note correctly explains the remaining choices.

claims.claim: The new auto-labeling policy applies SharePoint library default sensitivity labels to existing files.
claims.quote: create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in and does nothing to existing files until an administrator creates and enables the policy.
claims.quote:
After an administrator creates and enables this policy:

- Auto-labeling will evaluate existing files in selected SharePoint document libraries.

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling is included in eligible subscriptions rather than having a separately documented entitlement for this policy subtype.
claims.quote: | Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included | Included |

Select **+ Create auto-labeling policy**.

claims.claim: In Purview, Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy activates labeling after simulation.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**.
When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the **Turn on policy** option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -Mode Enable enables actions for an existing auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote:
The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify.
The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the auto-labeling policy.
Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Without a required activation role, Turn on policy is greyed out even after simulation succeeds.
claims.quote: Without one of these roles, the **Turn on policy** button appears greyed out even after a successful simulation.

claims.claim: Purview Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details opens policy review pages.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**. Select a policy, then select **View details** in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -IncludeProgressFeedback reports SharePoint or OneDrive labeling progress.
claims.quote:
The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to view.
IncludeProgressFeedback specifies whether to include the labeling progress of files in SharePoint or OneDrive. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.

claims.claim: The maximum daily labeling throughput is not a guaranteed processing rate.

claims.claim: PDFs are skipped entirely unless tenant PDF labeling support is enabled.
